claims.claim: Alcoa's structural role links bauxite and alumina conversion to primary aluminum supply for transport, construction, power and industrial needs; the South32 asset acquisition can deepen upstream resource control and supply-chain integration if acquired assets perform as expected.

The core bottlenecks are low-cost bauxite/alumina availability, reliable refining/smelting operations and competitive energy; successor bottlenecks shift toward integration execution, energy cost and operational stability rather than simple resource ownership.

causalEdges: industrial/electrification demand -> aluminum demand -> alumina/bauxite requirement -> integrated Alcoa asset utilization
upstream asset acquisition -> resource/control depth -> potential supply resilience/cost position
refinery disruption or high energy cost -> lower production/higher unit cost -> weaker margin and supply reliability
falsifiers: Acquired assets fail to improve supply resilience or cost position after integration.
Persistent refinery/smelter instability prevents Alcoa from converting favorable commodity conditions into reliable production.

claims.claim: Record financial results coexist with reduced alumina production guidance from operational instability; the contradiction is material because favorable pricing can mask reliability weakness and should remain for Resolver adjudication.

Debt issued to fund acquisition consideration increases fixed obligations while cash generation remains exposed to commodity prices, energy costs and refinery performance; strategic resource expansion therefore carries financing and integration fragility.

contradictions.contradiction: Record financial results coexist with reduced alumina production guidance from operational instability.

unknowns: pace and magnitude of synergy realization
